title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 5th District
area: Middle Tennessee, including Nashville-area and surrounding counties, under the congressional map Tennessee redrew in May 2026.

context.text: Tennessee redrew its congressional district boundaries in May 2026 (mid-decade redistricting); the filing deadline for U.S. House seats was reopened until May 15, 2026 after the new map was signed into law.
Incumbent Rep. Andy Ogles (R) lost the August 6, 2026 Republican primary to Charlie Hatcher, 53.3% to 46.7% (36,085 to 31,626 votes), so he is not on the November 3 general-election ballot.
Chaz Molder, mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, won the Democratic primary with 40.9% of the vote in a five-candidate field.
Race ratings as of September 2026: Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rate the race Solid Republican; Decision Desk and Sabato's Crystal Ball rate it Safe Republican.

candidates.name: Chaz Molder
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6 Democratic primary with 40.9% of the vote

summary.text: Chaz Molder is the mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, an attorney first elected mayor in 2018 and re-elected in 2022; he announced he would not seek a third term. A University of Tennessee and University of Memphis law school graduate, he is the Democratic nominee for the open 5th District seat and is running on lowering costs, health care access and labor protections.

background.text: Born and raised in Tennessee; a graduate of Columbia Central High School and, in his words, a product of Columbia's public schools.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, in 2005 and a law degree from the University of Memphis Cecil C. Humphreys School of Law in 2009.
Works as an attorney, according to Ballotpedia.
Elected mayor of Columbia in 2018 with 65 percent of the vote; his campaign website says he was then the youngest mayor in Tennessee and in the city's 200-plus-year history.
Won a second term as mayor in 2022 with just under 60 percent of the vote, then announced he would not run for a third term.
According to his campaign website, as mayor he has passed eight balanced budgets with no property tax increases and says he saved taxpayers $10.5 million through fiscal management.
Formed the Columbia Mayor's Youth Council as mayor.
Won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary for the 5th District with 40.9 percent of the vote.
According to his campaign website, he is married to Elizabeth Molder, they have three children in local public schools, and the family attends First United Methodist Church in Columbia.

priorities.text: Says he will advocate for a ban on stock trading by members of Congress, calling it a matter of ethics and accountability.
Says he is dedicated to lowering costs for Tennessee families, farmers, and seniors, including healthcare, housing, and grocery costs, and to strengthening labor protections.
Says he is committed to lowering healthcare costs and supporting rural hospitals so they can stay open.

record.text: As mayor of Columbia, passed eight consecutive balanced budgets without a property tax increase.

candidates.researchNotes: The minimum_wage entry was removed: his site only says he will stand up for the right to organize and strengthen labor protections, without mentioning wages.

candidates.name: Charlie Hatcher
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated incumbent Rep. Andy Ogles in the August 6 Republican primary, 53.3% to 46.7%

summary.text: Charlie Hatcher is a veterinarian and dairy farmer who served as Tennessee State Veterinarian and then, from 2019 to 2025, as Tennessee Commissioner of Agriculture. He defeated incumbent Rep. Andy Ogles in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary and is the Republican nominee for the 5th District.

background.text: A fifth-generation Tennessee farmer; his Ballotpedia biography says he operated the family's seventh-generation dairy farm in College Grove, Tennessee, established in 1847.
Holds a bachelor's degree in animal science from Middle Tennessee State University and a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.
Has more than 20 years in veterinary practice, specializing in livestock; his campaign website says he started eight businesses, including Hatcher Family Dairy, and describes him as an author.
Served as Tennessee State Veterinarian for about a decade before being appointed Commissioner of Agriculture by Gov. Bill Lee; he took office January 1, 2019, and left September 30, 2025.

Held national leadership roles, including past president of the American Association of Bovine Practitioners, the National Assembly of State Animal Health Officials, the United States Animal Health Association and the Southern Association of State Departments of Agriculture, and chaired the National Association of State Departments of Agriculture's Animal Agriculture Committee.
Has served on the University of Tennessee Board of Trustees and the Tennessee Board of Regents.

Launched his 5th District campaign on November 4, 2025, at Battle Mountain Farm in College Grove, and won the Republican primary over incumbent Andy Ogles on August 6, 2026, 53.3 percent to 46.7 percent.

priorities.text: Ran on his professional and government background: "He's a livestock veterinarian, started eight successful businesses from scratch including the Hatcher Family Dairy. ... For the past seven years he's served Tennessee as the Ag Commissioner."
priorities.quote: He's a livestock veterinarian, started eight successful businesses from scratch including the Hatcher Family Dairy. He's an author, Christian family man. For the past seven years he's served Tennessee as the Ag Commissioner. ... You want something hard done right? Hire a farmer.

priorities.text: Said he would prioritize making the federal government run more efficiently.

positions.summary: His campaign platform says he would oppose efforts by Washington to create unnecessary restrictions on responsible gun ownership.
positions.quote: oppose efforts by Washington to create unnecessary restrictions on responsible gun ownership

record.text: Served as Tennessee Commissioner of Agriculture from 2019 to 2025, appointed by Gov. Bill Lee.

candidates.researchNotes: His platform page mentions border security, an all-of-the-above energy strategy and "the sanctity of human life" in general terms; only the Second Amendment statement qualified as a position.

candidates.name: James Johnson

summary.text: James Johnson is an independent candidate on the November 3 general-election ballot for Tennessee's 5th District. Ballotpedia lists no campaign website, biography, or Candidate Connection survey response for him, and he polled 1% in an August 2026 Impact Research survey.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, biography, or public statements found for James Johnson beyond his name appearing on the ballot and in one poll.
